payload.title: 0.4.0 regression: HTTP email-auth response is flat, breaks native SDK decoders
payload.description:
frick-server 0.4.0's email signup/login HTTP response flattens the session fields at the top level, but the Swift (and Kotlin) SDK decoders expect the wrapped `{ session, user, isNewUser }` envelope the pre-rewrite TypeScript server returned. Every native-client signUp/signIn fails to decode -> auth is fully broken for the Swift/Kotlin SDKs against 0.4.0.

Caught by RangerCRM's localhost integration suite during the 0.4.0 migration (RCRM-165): 68/383 tests failed, all with `DecodingError.keyNotFound: Key 'session' not found` thrown from `FrickClient.signUpWithEmail` in test setUp.

## Evidence

frick-server 0.4.0 `POST /auth/email/signup` returns (crates/frick-server/src/auth_routes.rs `mint_email_session_response`, ~line 889):
```json
{ "schemaHash":..., "sessionToken":..., "tenantId":..., "userId":..., "displayName":..., "email":..., "handle":..., "deviceId":..., "replicaId":..., "expiresAt":..., "isNewUser": true }
```

FrickSwift 0.4.0 decodes (FrickClient.swift):
```swift
private struct SignInWithEmailEnvelope: Decodable {
    let session: FrickSession   // <- expects a nested `session` object
    let user: [String: FrickJSONValue]
    let isNewUser: Bool
}
```
where `FrickSession` = `{ schemaHash?, sessionToken, tenantId?, userId, displayName?, handle?, deviceId, replicaId, expiresAt }`. `SignInWithAppleEnvelope` and `SignInWithGoogleEnvelope` are the same wrapped shape.

## Why it slipped through

The conformance fixtures (conformance/fixtures/wire/manifest.json) pin the WebSocket wire only — the HTTP auth-endpoint response shapes are not covered. The web client (@fricken/core) doesn't decode the HTTP signup response (it's WS-first), so only the native SDKs are affected and nothing caught the divergence.

## Fix

Return the wrapped envelope from all auth responders (email signup + login, Apple, Google, OIDC, generic signup/login): `{ session: { schemaHash, sessionToken, tenantId, userId, displayName, handle, deviceId, replicaId, expiresAt }, user: { id/userId, displayName, email, handle }, isNewUser }`. Confirmed locally: nesting the existing fields under `session` + adding a `user` object makes RangerCRM's Swift suite decode auth and proceed (validation patch on a local Frick branch).

Add an HTTP-auth-envelope conformance fixture so this shape is pinned going forward, not just the WS wire.

## Downstream

RangerCRM is on the 0.4.0 stack (RCRM-165) and is fully migrated except this blocker; it will re-pin once a fixed frick-server ships (0.4.1). Until then RangerCRM's CI must run against a locally-patched server.
